76	- Minimal option: ordenar os change sets por data do commit
77	- Selected option: ordem topológica das histórias das cabeças (`git rev-list --topo-order -n 1`)
78	- Rationale: commits do mesmo segundo (comuns em lotes e testes) empatam por data; a ordem topológica lista um descendente antes dos seus ancestrais e não depende de relógio
79	- Consequences: se as cabeças divergem (nenhuma descende de todas) vale a primeira da ordem topológica, uma cabeça entre as mais novas

This is round 2. The code hasn't changed since round 1. The diff from `f966dfeb` to `c94d2da7` touches only `.pose/` records: indexes, the round-1 bundle and run records, and the start file. So the four round-1 findings are still there. All four are low severity and go forward as accepted follow-ups. Round 1 was refused only because `artifact-check` hadn't been run. I ran it this time and it exited 0, reporting 941 items, all of them repo-wide "orphan" warnings.

## What I checked
- **The fix** (`pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:783-794`, `:4468-4490`): the head is now picked as the first commit from `git rev-list --topo-order -n 1 <heads>`. That commit is always one of the input heads and no other input head descends from it, because any non-input commit is an ancestor of some input and would be listed later. The choice works whatever order the change sets are in, and a commit that isn't a full 40-character object id gives an empty result, which keeps the old head. A scope with a single head never calls Git, so spec scopes behave exactly as before.
- **Sealed bundles keep their recorded head:** `reviewBundleSubject` is only called when a bundle is prepared (`review_bundle.go:522`) and from `review_structure.go:118`. Every check that uses the head compares the stored `Bundle.Payload.Subject.Head` and never recomputes it (`review_dispatch.go:543,1165,1534`, `review_run_provenance.go:755`, `review_run_continuity.go:390`, `delegation_handoff.go:312`). The bundle digest clears `Subject.Head`, `Base` and `ChangeSets` (`review_bundle.go:1963-1965`), so the new head doesn't change bundle identity.
- **Head source:** `ResolvedHead` is read from the delivery-integrity index (`delivery_integrity.go:51`) and isn't validated before it reaches `rev-list` (R1-F1).
- **Side note:** `artifact-check` resolved the change set `cs-9d0a5e7baf55` with head `2f525e14`. That commit is a descendant of the reviewed head, and it isn't an ancestor of `c94d2da7`. It's the commit that sealed this round's bundle. It's expected and isn't a defect.

## Prior findings
- **R1-F1:** not fixed. `review_bundle.go:4482` still has no `--` and doesn't validate the heads.
- **R1-F2:** not fixed. When heads diverge, one tip is still picked without any warning.
- **R1-F3:** not fixed. There is still no test that calls `reviewBundleSubject` with several change sets.
- **R1-F4:** not fixed. Falling back to the last set's head still leaves no warning or reason in the bundle.

## New finding
- **N1 (low)**, `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:786`: `Subject.Base` still comes from the first change set by id, the same arbitrary choice this spec fixes for the head. The brief's displayed range (`review_brief.go:316`) and the design-delta range (`design_delta.go:184,269`) now pair the newest head with an arbitrary base. That range can leave out commits of members whose base is older.

This is round 2. The code hasn't changed since round 1. The diff from `f966dfeb` to `c94d2da7` touches only `.pose/` records: indexes, the round-1 bundle and run records, and the start file. So the four round-1 findings are still there. All four are low severity and go forward as accepted follow-ups. Round 1 was refused only because `artifact-check` hadn't been run. I ran it this time and it exited 0, reporting 941 items, all of them repo-wide "orphan" warnings.

## What I checked
- **The fix** (`pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:783-794`, `:4468-4490`): the head is now picked as the first commit from `git rev-list --topo-order -n 1 <heads>`. That commit is always one of the input heads and no other input head descends from it, because any non-input commit is an ancestor of some input and would be listed later. The choice works whatever order the change sets are in, and a commit that isn't a full 40-character object id gives an empty result, which keeps the old head. A scope with a single head never calls Git, so spec scopes behave exactly as before.
- **Sealed bundles keep their recorded head:** `reviewBundleSubject` is only called when a bundle is prepared (`review_bundle.go:522`) and from `review_structure.go:118`. Every check that uses the head compares the stored `Bundle.Payload.Subject.Head` and never recomputes it (`review_dispatch.go:543,1165,1534`, `review_run_provenance.go:755`, `review_run_continuity.go:390`, `delegation_handoff.go:312`). The bundle digest clears `Subject.Head`, `Base` and `ChangeSets` (`review_bundle.go:1963-1965`), so the new head doesn't change bundle identity.
- **Head source:** `ResolvedHead` is read from the delivery-integrity index (`delivery_integrity.go:51`) and isn't validated before it reaches `rev-list` (R1-F1).
- **Side note:** `artifact-check` resolved the change set `cs-9d0a5e7baf55` with head `2f525e14`. That commit is a descendant of the reviewed head, and it isn't an ancestor of `c94d2da7`. It's the commit that sealed this round's bundle. It's expected and isn't a defect.

## Prior findings
- **R1-F1:** not fixed. `review_bundle.go:4482` still has no `--` and doesn't validate the heads.
- **R1-F2:** not fixed. When heads diverge, one tip is still picked without any warning.
- **R1-F3:** not fixed. There is still no test that calls `reviewBundleSubject` with several change sets.
- **R1-F4:** not fixed. Falling back to the last set's head still leaves no warning or reason in the bundle.

## New finding
- **N1 (low)**, `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:786`: `Subject.Base` still comes from the first change set by id, the same arbitrary choice this spec fixes for the head. The brief's displayed range (`review_brief.go:316`) and the design-delta range (`design_delta.go:184,269`) now pair the newest head with an arbitrary base. That range can leave out commits of members whose base is older.
